> [!NOTE]
> **Manage Microsoft Graph connections with profiles and a redesigned desktop.**

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Release type** | Feature |
| **Upgrade priority** | Recommended |
| **Breaking changes** | Windows storage locations and active-profile defaults; see [Upgrade guidance](#upgrade-guidance) |
| **Python support** | Python 3.10+ (`>=3.10`) |

## Highlights

- **Organize multiple connections** — Create, rename, select, and remove named profiles, each with its own configuration and token cache. Choose an active connection or leave the Connections Manager empty after removing all profiles.
- **A redesigned desktop experience** — A new Home page leads into the Connections Manager, with a dark interface, scalable service logos, startup progress, and navigation back to the main menu.
- **Test saved connections** — Run optional connection tests, cancel a pending test, and review result indicators. Device-code sign-in includes helpers for copying the code and opening the sign-in page. Results describe completed tests, not continuous connection monitoring.
- **Help where it is needed** — Contextual drawers explain connection settings and application features. Terms of Use and Privacy Policy can be read inside the application, including bundled offline copies.
- **Optional app shortcuts** — Create a personal launcher from Home or Connections on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Installation does not create shortcuts automatically; launchers require the current Python environment to remain installed.
- **Select profiles from Python** — Profile-management helpers and the `Authentication(profile=...)` option let applications choose a saved connection explicitly.

## Fixed

- Authentication-method selections are now saved with connection settings and restored when the profile is reopened, rather than reverting to the default selection.
- Fixed saved-credential loading through `Build.Default()` so authentication-method settings do not cause a credential-builder error.
- Fixed Windows taskbar identity setup for long installation paths by shortening the relaunch command when needed.
- Fixed saved-profile buttons overlapping the heading and Add button while a connection test is running.

## Changed

- Updated the desktop application with refreshed visuals and improved navigation.
- Microsoft Graph is the only available desktop provider. Azure Key Vault, Dataverse / Dynamics 365, Azure Storage, Azure SQL, and Exchange Online can be selected for preview, but their Continue action displays **Currently Unavailable** and remains disabled.
- Removing a profile archives its local configuration and token-cache files rather than securely erasing them. Shared client secrets remain in the operating system's credential store.
- Package metadata now identifies azauthlib as Production/Stable rather than Beta.
- Requires certifi 2026.10.19 or newer to address [PYSEC-2026-4320](https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2).

## Upgrade guidance

These notes compare this update with the latest published version, **1.4.0b1**.

> [!WARNING]
> On Windows, default configuration and cache locations have changed. Existing files are not automatically migrated from the previous location. Back up existing settings before upgrading, then recreate the required connections in the Connections Manager. Another sign-in may be required.

Follow the [upgrade instructions](https://github.com/doydl-technologies/azauthlib#upgrading-from-140b1) before replacing an existing installation.

When no profile is supplied, new authentication instances use the active profile. Applications that require a particular connection should pass `profile=` explicitly. If every profile has been removed, create a profile before constructing an authentication instance.

Profile removal does not revoke tokens, sign out an account everywhere, or remove shared client secrets from the operating system's credential store.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade azauthlib==4.17.6
```

For optional first-time setup using the graphical interface, run `azauthlib-app` in the
environment where azauthlib is installed. Credentials can also be configured through
Python or environment variables; the application is not required.
